newsitem.title: USA: Edison has not set San Onofre 3 restart.
newsitem.headline: Edison has not set San Onofre 3 restart.

text.p: Edison International said Tuesday the company has not set a restart schedule for unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear generating complex in San Clemente, Calif., which was shut earlier today for repairs.
"We don't have an estimate. We have to conduct a root cause analysis," said company spokesman Ray Golden.
Plant engineers detected a leak in the reactor's coolant piping system and began ramping down the 1,080 megawatt (MW) unit at 0400 (PDT), he said.
Repairs on unit 3 will not affect the operation of the facility's 1,070 MW unit 2, he said.
"Unit 2 is up, and running at full power," Golden said.
Despite the unplanned outage of San Onofre 3, Edison International has adequate generation capacity to meet customer power demand, he said.
Edison International, the operator, has a 75 percent stake in both San Onofre units, while San Diego Gas & Electric, a subsidiary of Enova Corp has, has 20 percent.
The remaining five percent is split between the southern California cities of Anaheim and Riverside.
